correctness.rationale: Smoothness follows from p∤n and D_n(-2)=-2; the tame quotient of w²=t^(2n)+1 identifies invariant differentials. Hyperelliptic Cartier coefficients are nonzero binomial residues, so the Cartier map is a partial permutation on the cover. The fixed-point-free involution θ(i)=min(±p i modulo 2n) pairs active/inactive rows, and i↔n−i halves the count on the quotient, yielding exactly (n−1)/4. Direct residue argument gives Cartier²=0. The six-case exact modular verifier passed including p=13,n=17 and p=31,n=13; finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the exact first Cartier rank g/2 and a-number g/2 of X_n in the p² ≡ -1 (mod 2n) family. The directly relevant 2019 quotient and 2026 automorphism/maximality proofs give the family but no first-rank formula; the 2008 general maximality–Cartier nilpotence implies C²=0 but cannot determine rank(C). Novoselov computes a related covering-curve Cartier matrix and Tafazolian–Top 2025 treats y²=D_n; neither states the half-rank on this quotient. published-finding corpus searches for the formulas and aliases had no matching claim; historical priority remains qualified and one 2025 full article was not inspected.

value.rationale: The recently identified maximal hyperelliptic family is distinguished by minimal geometric automorphism group, but maximality alone yields only p-rank zero and nilpotent Cartier powers. The exact first-rank and a-number determine a genuinely finer p-torsion invariant, distinguish non-superspecial maximal examples (genus six a=3), and show the nilpotence bound is attained with rank half the genus in infinite arithmetic families.
